verdict.rationale: Devin CLI documents a permission system that covers both built-in and MCP tools, with access controllable 'at multiple levels'. That is a first-party mechanism for governing what the agent may do, but the evidence does not describe distinct autonomy tiers or which actions skip manual confirmation. missing for 10: explicit tiered autonomy modes (e.g. ask/auto-approve/full-auto), documentation of which actions need confirmation at each tier, org-level admin enforcement by an engineering lead, coverage beyond the CLI (cloud/web sessions), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can set tiered autonomy levels controlling what an agent can do without manual confirmation

citations.quote: MCP tools are subject to the same permission system as built-in tools. You can control access at multiple levels
